metadata.title: The analytical value of non-probability samples in the context of TALIS (EN)

extraction.outcome_summary: The working paper reviewed established uses of non-probability samples in comparative, cross-national surveys and assessed what lessons they might offer for TALIS. It concluded that non-probability sampling would be unsuitable for the TALIS main survey because of bias and the inability to quantify uncertainty, but it could be useful for complementary longitudinal modules, field-trial-related development work, or exploratory outreach surveys. The paper emphasized that any such use would require careful attention to theoretically grounded confounders, controlled recruitment, post hoc weighting where feasible, and transparent reporting of limitations. It also noted that TALIS’s existing probability-based design and relatively high response rates make it a strong reference point for any non-probability component.
